newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Bildt defines post-election strategy for Bosnia.
newsitem.headline: Bildt defines post-election strategy for Bosnia.

text.p: Carl Bildt, the international community's representative in Bosnia, said on Friday his priority would be to set up common institutions as soon as possible after the September 14 elections.

Bildt said he had already held intensive discussions with the candidates for a three-man rotating national presidency and said he hoped they would be able to assume legal authority for the country within days of the polls being certified legal.

"Say 10 days or something like that we will try immediately to bring the three members of the presidency together for the first time at which they will assume the legal authority for the country," he told reporters.
Bildt was speaking after meeting NATO ambassadors to bring them up to date with the preparation for the September 14 polls for local and national presidencies and assemblies.
Bildt said the international community would have to make a "concerted and sustained" effort throughout the autumn if the common institutions foreseen in the Dayton peace accords actually take shape.
"It is highly complex, it is a question of bringing together people who have been fighting war against each other... and getting them to work together," he said.
Bildt has drawn up a "quick-start package" of core legislation for the new multi-ethnic, decentralised state envisaged by Dayton to be implemented as soon as possible after the elections.

Diplomats say the plan would be to pass a state budget, adopt laws governing Bosnia's international economic relations and citizenship, create a central bank, set a two-year duration of parliamentary mandates and agree provisional air traffic regulations.
Bildt also plans to try to bring together the 42 directly-elected members of a new House of Represenatives in early October and begin negotiations on the formation of a council of ministers.
"We have to get going quickly to avoid accusations the polls are just cementing the ethnic divisions," said one diplomatic source.

Candidates will be elected to cantonal offices on the federation side and to the office of the Presidency of the Serb republic on the republic side; to republic and federation parliaments; to a national parliament and to a three-member national Presidency.
